$comment: The cross-viewer visual checklist, in the form the vision model is asked to answer.
This is the machine-readable version of what the manual pass checked by eye when a
human opened each staged PDF in Acrobat and Bluebeam. Each item must be answerable
from a single rendered page image alone - anything needing the annotation dictionary
belongs in src-tauri/tests/bb_interop_conformance.rs (the PRIMARY, structural check),
and anything needing the viewer's own report belongs in the Acrobat leg's JSON.

items.question: Does this page render actual content, or is it blank/white/garbled? Answer BLANK only if the page is essentially empty.
Are annotation markups (shapes, lines, clouds, text notes, stamps, measurements) visibly drawn on the page? Roughly how many distinct markups can you count?

Do any markups render as empty rectangles, hollow placeholder boxes, or boxes containing only a label where artwork or content is expected? This specifically catches the stamp-renders-as-empty-box defect.
Is text inside text-bearing markups (notes, callouts, free text, measurement labels) legible and correctly positioned, rather than clipped, overlapping, or reduced to boxes?
If measurement markups are present, are their dimension labels readable and attached to the right geometry?
Do all markups sit within the page area and appear positioned over the drawing content, rather than shifted off-page, stacked in a corner, or mirrored?
